claim: Experimental human hair-follicle systems support a directional path from excessive CTS mechanical contraction through PIEZO1-associated mechanotransduction to progenitor apoptosis/depletion and impaired follicle growth.

evidence_chain.input: MCH-induced CTS contraction in cultured human anagen hair follicles
observations: dose-dependent hair-growth retardation and anagen-maintenance impairment
dose-dependent CD34-positive progenitor loss and apoptosis
improved growth retardation and premature catagen induction
restored matrix/ORS proliferation relative to MCH challenge

evidence_chain.rescue: GPR133 knockdown or ML-7 reversed the contractile/pathological effects

HF01_mapping.directional_support: M perturbation -> P injury and H-function impairment; M inhibition -> partial rescue

not_supported: ECM/EMT transcript state E is identical to CTS contraction M
all human AGA progenitor loss is caused by M
M is an in-vivo clinical biomarker
M inhibition establishes full follicle recoverability
experimental rescue proves absence of a deeper hysteretic lock

model_update: HF-SIM-028 remains correct as a generic observational non-identifiability theorem. The external intervention evidence now selects M->P as one biologically supported directional mechanism for the mechanical state M, while E<->P and E<->M remain unresolved.
